obligation: FD&C Act section 524B: ensuring cybersecurity of devices
basis: Section 524B(a) covers anyone who submits a 510(k), PMA, PDP, De Novo or HDE for a cyber device. The VM-7 510(k), IP-4 510(k) and AI-001 De Novo were all submitted after the 2023-03-29 effective date, and the planned AI-002 510(k) will be too. No size exemption. VM-5 (cleared 2018) is not reached by 524B (Pub. L. 117-328 section 3305(d)) but stays under the QMSR, MDR and correction rules

obligation: Quality Management System Regulation (QMSR)
citation: 21 CFR Part 820 (ISO 13485 incorporated by reference; effective 2026-02-02)
basis: The company is a registered manufacturer of class II devices

obligation: Medical device reporting
basis: Registered manufacturer with devices in use at about 290 hospitals; about 4 MDRs a month

obligation: Corrections and removals
basis: Registered manufacturer; field actions and cybersecurity updates for devices in use

obligation: FDA premarket (2026-02-03) and postmarket (December 2016) cybersecurity guidance
applies: Nonbinding, used as FDA's stated expectations
basis: FDA uses the guidance to judge whether a submission gives a reasonable assurance of cybersecurity; the postmarket guidance sets the conditions for enforcement discretion on 806 reports for uncontrolled risk

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule (business associate)
basis: The company holds BAAs with about 290 hospitals, and the CCC creates, receives, maintains and transmits PHI for them, so the company is a business associate (45 CFR 160.103) and the Security Rule applies (164.302). No size exemption; 164.306(b) affects how, not whether. The company is not a covered entity

obligation: HIPAA Privacy Rule (business associate duties)
applies: Yes, through the BAAs (not analyzed in P03)
basis: Business associate privacy duties flow through the hospital BAAs and are handled by the Compliance and Privacy Officer

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (business associate notice)
basis: Same business associate status; 164.410 governs notice to the hospitals, and the BAAs can set shorter terms

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule NPRM (2025)
basis: Not a final rule; tracked for planning

obligation: Section 1557: patient care decision support tools
applies: Not to the company directly (applies to hospital deployers)
basis: 45 CFR 92.210 binds covered entities that use patient care decision support tools. AI-001 is used by 22 hospitals; the company supplies subgroup performance data to support their duty

obligation: HIPAA group health plan requirements
basis: The employee health plan is fully insured. The broker confirmed in P03 fieldwork that the company, as plan sponsor, receives only summary health information and enrollment and disenrollment information, which 164.314(b)(1) excludes

obligation: DFARS 252.204-7012 Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting
basis: The contract register shows hospital, health system and group purchasing customers only; no defense contracts

obligation: CMMC Program rule and DFARS 252.204-7021
basis: No defense contracts

obligation: ITAR
basis: The products are civilian medical devices listed with FDA; no defense articles

obligation: EAR
basis: All sales are to U.S. customers; export classification of products and technology is outside these samples

obligation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and related federal contract clauses
basis: No federal contracts

obligation: SEC cybersecurity incident and governance disclosure rules
basis: The company is privately held

obligation: Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act
basis: No final rule. The proposed criteria would reach manufacturers of class II and III devices (proposed 6 CFR 226.2(b)(11)(iii)), so it is rechecked when final

obligation: NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3, Guide to OT Security
basis: No federal rule binds the plant's OT security; the manufacturing overlay recommends SP 800-82 Rev. 3 where no binding rule applies

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (third-party agent notice)
basis: The company maintains computerized data in the CCC for hospitals, about 80 of them in Florida, so it is a third-party agent that must notify the hospital no later than 10 days after determining a breach

obligation: Breach and third-party agent notice laws of other states
citation: Each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Hospital customers are in 24 states

obligation: Hospital BAA notice and security terms
basis: Notice terms vary by hospital, some as short as 5 business days

obligation: CCC service agreements: availability commitment
basis: 99.9% monthly availability with service credits of up to 25% of monthly fees

obligation: Group purchasing organization contract: SOC 2 scope
basis: The contract, covering about 60 of the company's hospitals, requires a SOC 2 report with Availability and Confidentiality
